articles.title: Retinal Vessel Volume Density and Intraoperative Cortical Vascular Phenotypes in Moyamoya Disease
articles.content: Background Angiographic staging describes large-artery stenosis and collateral evolution in moyamoya disease but does not directly depict the cortical surface vasculature, which can vary among patients with similar Suzuki stages. We examined whether a side-matched three-dimensional retinal vascular measure was associated with intraoperative cortical vascular phenotypes after accounting for Suzuki stage. Methods This prospective single-center cohort included 52 patients with moyamoya disease who underwent combined direct and indirect revascularization; 48 had analyzable retinal vessel volume density (RVVD) in the side-matched eye. RVVD was defined as the percentage of the corresponding retinal tissue volume occupied by three-dimensional optical coherence tomography angiography vascular signal within the central 6 x 6-mm region from the retinal nerve fiber layer to the inner plexiform layer. After dural opening and before vascular manipulation, overall cortical vascular richness and arterial, venous, and small-vessel richness were graded from 0 to 3. Associations were evaluated with Spearman correlation and proportional-odds ordinal logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, and ipsilateral Suzuki stage. Results Mean RVVD was 12.92% (SD, 3.30 percentage points). Higher RVVD was associated with greater overall cortical vascular richness ({rho} =0.523; bias-corrected and accelerated bootstrap 95% CI, 0.279-0.714; P<0.001) and arterial richness ({rho} =0.522; 95% CI, 0.261-0.714; P<0.001). Per 1-SD higher RVVD, the adjusted cumulative odds ratio for being in a higher richness category was 3.92 (95% CI, 1.82-8.44; P<0.001) for overall cortical vascular richness and 4.31 (95% CI, 1.92-9.70; P<0.001) for arterial richness. Conclusions In moyamoya disease, higher side-matched RVVD was associated with richer overall and arterial cortical vascular phenotypes at revascularization surgery, independent of Suzuki stage. Three-dimensional retinal vascular imaging may therefore provide a noninvasive, side-specific preoperative measure of cortical vascular remodeling.

articles.title: Early locus coeruleus tauopathy features potassium channel dysfunction and is attenuated by Kv7 activation
articles.content: Background The locus coeruleus (LC) accumulates abnormal tau early in Alzheimer's disease, yet the mechanisms linking early tauopathy to neuronal dysfunction and the potential to modify subsequent pathology remain unclear. We investigated potassium-dependent excitability control, associated molecular 5 changes and Kv7-targeted intervention. Methods We combined electrophysiology, single-cell RNA sequencing, immunohistochemistry and sleep-electroencephalographic recordings in P301S tau transgenic (PS19) mice and wild-type mice receiving local LC inoculation of synthetic human tau fibrils. Pharmacological channel modulation and glycogen synthase kinase- 3 (GSK- 3) inhibition assessed pharmacological modulation of the electrophysiological phenotype. Chronic retigabine treatment assessed pathological outcomes after unilateral locus coeruleus fibril inoculation in young PS19 mice. Results Young, but not aged, PS19 mice exhibited elevated tonic firing and intrinsic excitability of locus 15 coeruleus neurons, associated with pre-tangle phosphorylated tau accumulation and reduced low-threshold potassium current density. Exploratory single-cell profiling identified candidate expression changes in marker-defined noradrenergic neurons: increased stress-associated gene expression coincided with reduced expression of neurofilament, neuronal-maintenance and potassium-channel genes, including Kcnq3 and Kcnd1. Increased nuclear RE-1 silencing 20 transcription factor (REST) and reduced Kv7.2 and Kv7.3 immunoreactivity suggested a candidate transcriptional mechanism associated with channel dysfunction. Local fibril inoculation reproduced the physiological abnormalities in wild-type mice, with hyperexcitability depending on endogenous tau. Combined Kv4/Kv7 modulation attenuated hyperexcitability, while GSK- 3; inhibition reduced tau phosphorylation, increased low-threshold potassium currents and lowered tonic firing. Both models showed increased dark-phase wakefulness and state-dependent electroencephalographic power changes. Chronic treatment with the Kv7 opener retigabine reduced bilateral LC AT8-positive tau burden and was associated with higher tyrosine hydroxylase (TH)-positive neuronal density after unilateral seeding. Conclusions Early LC tauopathy combines impaired potassium channel-dependent excitability control with transcriptional changes consistent with cellular stress and reduced neuronal maintenance. Kv7 activation attenuates seeded tau pathology, supporting excitability regulation as a candidate intervention strategy during early tauopathy.

articles.title: Overexpression of α synuclein in Midbrain Dopamine Neurons Drives Learning Deficits in Mice
articles.content: Parkinson disease (PD) is diagnosed based on core motor features. However, changes in cognitive function are often already present. Cognitive symptoms include changes in executive function, including organization, planning, multi-tasking, and flexible decision-making. These early cognitive deficits have been difficult to model and remain understudied. Here, we investigated whether AAV-based overexpression of wild-type human alpha-synuclein (syn) in midbrain dopaminergic neurons can produce deficits in learning and behavioral flexibility. We found that syn mice develop progressive impairment in basic action-outcome learning. In addition, we found that syn mice show impairments in behavioral flexibility during probabilistic reversal learning. Together, these findings demonstrate that syn overexpression in midbrain dopaminergic neurons is sufficient to drive cognitive decline. Our early-stage PD model offers a temporal window to dissect cellular and circuits mechanisms underlying non-motor manifestations of PD.

articles.title: Chronic stress reduces behavioural flexibility and autonomic adaptation when aversive outcomes are controllable
articles.content: Chronic stress is associated with altered adaptation to threat, yet its effects on aversive learning under varying threat predictability and controllability remain unclear. Thirty participants with chronic stress and thirty healthy controls completed a task to learn how well visual cues predicted upcoming electric shocks (predictability) and whether correct predictions of shocks could reduce shock intensity (controllability). We found that, for controllable conditions, accuracy was similar across varying degrees of predictability in the chronic stress group, whereas accuracy in the healthy control group was highest in highly predictable blocks. The chronic stress group responded more slowly than controls and their skin conductance responses were generally lower and indistinguishable across predictability and controllability. We used a computational model to estimate subjective uncertainty and related these estimates to behavioural responses and skin conductance. Modelling showed that controllability shaped uncertainty differently across groups. In chronic stress, with control, subjective stress reflected uncertainty about likely outcomes, reaction time reflected changing outcome probabilities, and skin conductance reflected unexpected outcomes. Without control, subjective stress reflected unexpected outcomes, reaction time uncertainty about likely outcomes, and skin conductance both unexpected outcomes and outcome uncertainty. In healthy controls, subjective stress reflected changing outcome probabilities with control and outcome uncertainty without control, whereas skin conductance showed the reverse pattern, and reaction time reflected likely outcomes only under control. Together, these findings indicate less adaptation in chronic stress, reflected in reduced modulation of reaction time by controllability and skin conductance by predictability and controllability, alongside altered uncertainty associations across response domains.
articles.author: Rajput, D., Felmingham, K., Sophie Lin, C.-H., Garrido, M. I.

articles.title: Neural mechanisms of lightness constancy
articles.content: Object-specific variables are entangled in sensory input. For example, lightness, whether a surface is white or black, not only depends on the surface reflectance but also on the incident illumination. The brain must thus perform inference to achieve a reliable percept of lightness irrespective of illumination (lightness constancy). Whether this results from simple luminance contrast operations early in the visual system or computations at higher levels remains unresolved. We find that neural lightness signals only appear in the extragranular layers of cortical Area V4, and dominate for shadow regions, as opposed to the comparison of local and surrounding luminance (simultaneous contrast). This suggests that lightness is computed downstream from simultaneous contrast, ruling out simple low-level mechanisms, and instead supporting mid-level anchoring theory.
articles.author: Didehvar, F., Vanstiphout, R., Cavanagh, P., Franken, T. P.

articles.title: Microglia and microglia activation are protective in an LSD1-induced model of neurodegeneration
articles.content: Attempts to determine the function of microglia activation and the immune system in neurodegenerative diseases have yielded conflicting results, with some data showing a protective effect, while other data shows a detrimental effect. This discrepancy in the function of microglia activation and the immune system in neurodegeneration likely stems from differing functions during the build-up of pathological proteins versus later stage defects. Therefore, we investigated the function of microglia activation and the immune system in Lsd1 inducible deletion mice, which serve as a late-stage tau-associated neurodegeneration model without the build-up of pathological proteins. We found that loss of LSD1 causes the morphological and transcriptional activation of microglia, accompanied by astrocyte activation and a broader immune response. Blocking microglia activation by inactivating Trem2 inhibited the entire Lsd1-induced immune response, while pharmacologically inhibiting microglia via PLX3397 treatment eliminated microglia but did not block astrocyte reactivity or the broader immune response. Surprisingly, despite these effects, neither blocking microglia activation nor depleting microglia prevented Lsd1-induced neurodegeneration, paralysis and death. Instead, we found in both cases that survival was significantly reduced. These results suggest that microglia and microglial activation, independent of astrocyte reactivity and the broader inflammatory response, is neuroprotective in a late-stage tau-associated neurodegeneration model.
articles.author: Bai, Y., Gosrani, S. P., Han, C., Fix, C. E., Katz, J., Beddingfield, Z., Jain, M., Gouveia-Silva, A., Engstrom, A. K., Soares, M. L., Katz, D. J.

articles.title: Neural competition predicts speech production advantages in congenital amusia
articles.content: Mental health research has traditionally been deficit-focused, and cognitive advantages in mental conditions have almost always been documented retrospectively. Here we propose and test an a priori pathway for predicting such advantages from a condition's impaired neural basis, neural competition and brain-mind associations. Using congenital amusia (CA), a neurodevelopmental disorder with a well-defined deficit in right frontotemporal circuit (FTC), as a model, we predicted that interhemispheric competition would release the left homologue from inhibition, conferring advantages in speech production. Two independent studies, multimodal neuroimaging and behavioral testing, confirmed this prediction: MRI revealed right FTC impairment alongside competitive-like benefits of the left FTC in CA; and CA showed speech production advantages with intact episodic memory and constrained music learning. These findings provide the first empirical demonstration that cognitive advantages can be predicted in advance and then verified, offering a principled, mechanism-based alternative to the deficit-focused paradigm.

articles.content:

Hu et al. showed that motor memory decay involves microglia engulfing memory-related myelin sheaths. Reduced engram activity lowers CD47, a ‘don’t eat me’ signal, thus promoting microglia-mediated myelin clearance and facilitating memory decay.

articles.title: Noise resilience in brain decoding driven by spiking neural networks for responsive robot control
articles.content: Brain computer interface (BCI) is a promising technology, expanding on many fields ranging from medical to commercial applications. The diffusion of this technique is compromised by the complexity of the treated data and the unavoidable presence of noise in those systems. This study contributes to the solution of this problem by proposing a BCI pipeline that relies on the use of spiking neural networks (SNNs), quantifying their robustness to noise in the context of brain decoding through the classification of Electroencephalography (EEG). We benchmark a shallow convolutional network against two spiking counterparts based on leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) and adaptive LIF neurons on the four-class BNCI 2014-001 motor imagery dataset. The conventional model has a slight advantage in clean conditions, but it degrades dramatically once the input is corrupted. In contrast, SNN demonstrates remarkable robustness under signal degradation. Under global Gaussian noise, CNN accuracy drops by 58.56%, whereas Adaptive LIF SNN accuracy drops by only 0.80%. Similarly, when trained on recordings with one electrode removed and tested on the complete montage, CNN loses 36.00% of its accuracy, compared with 0.34% for the SNN. With semi-simulated ocular, muscular and cardiac artifacts the gap is smaller, but the spiking models still degrade less than the CNN for every artifact type. This robustness is obtained at equal model size with 18.0 of the 24.6 MMAC required per trial by the baseline replaced by accumulate-only, spike-driven operations. Finally, the spiking model was integrated in a full decoding-to-actuation pipeline driving a Franka Emika Research 3 robot from a replayed EEG stream. These findings indicate that, compared with a dense counterpart, spiking computation substantially reduces the sensitivity of EEG decoding to signal corruption, which supports the use of SNNs in deployments where robustness matters more than peak accuracy.
